follow-up time: Postoperative follow-up, time frame not specified
study type: Retrospective analysis of prospectively collected data
exposure: unicornuate uterus with cavitated noncommunicating horn (class II B)
laparoscopic resection of the horn site of hematometra
outcome: Resolution of dysmenorrhea and pelvic pain
cohort: 19 women with unicornuate uterus with cavitated noncommunicating horn (class II B), of whom 5 underwent laparoscopic surgery
finding: Laparoscopic resection of the horn site of hematometra in cases of unicornuate uterus with a solidly attached rudimentary horn appears to be a safe and effective treatment option, leading to the resolution of symptoms and allowing for the possibility of future pregnancies.
gest_age: Two premature births at 34th and 36th week
